industry.why: Neutral, carried, balanced on new evidence both ways. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): two houses call a cyclical upturn, DNB Carnegie (22 Oct) reading Sandvik and Metso as a new mining cycle and Danske (18 Oct) heavy trucks and pulp and paper turning, and Goldman's economists (16 Oct) have US industrial production beating with machinery and electrical equipment near peak capacity use; against it, Danske's own warning that most cyclical exposure is 'more or less at all-time highs' with 'cost inflation emerging', a risk-off regime confirmed on all five defensive windows, and Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: D now, C prior at industry level. The sector rows do the work: Electrical equipment and grid, Diversified groups, Distributors and Test and measurement at C, Flow control and Building technology at D. Counter-case for B: the order data are the strongest non-AI demand read in the pack; for D: the tape and the regime.

sector.key: O.4. Electrical equipment, grid and automation
sector.why: Neutral, carried, with the two sides both stronger. The tape: Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: F now, B prior; the 16-Oct-26 reading was D, so the grade fell again. The demand: xAI calls power and cooling 'the primary bottleneck' (via Jefferies, 21 Oct), Goldman's economists (16 Oct) find electrical equipment and machinery near peak capacity use 'likely reflecting AI-related demand', and Nvidia's power-sharing system is an offset, not an end, to the constraint. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): grid programmes are debt-funded and the discount rate is still rising, so orders up, shares down, balanced. Two live holdings, Alfen (4.60%) and Arteche (3.28%), judged in component 4. Counter-case for D: two consecutive falls in relative strength are the market's answer; for B: the binding constraint on the largest capital-spending theme in the world is this sector's product. Moves to B if relative strength returns to B with the AI-infrastructure proxies recovering; to D on a further F reading with hyperscaler capital spending guides cut.

geography.why: Neutral, carried. No source spoke to Spain this week (a source pack is present, 2026-W43, and it carried nothing country-specific here), relative strength is not graded by country, and Richard's view is G10 and Europe-wide with no country line. An absence is an absence; no tilt.

judgement.heading: Arteche | Middle Innings Core Investment, no sell signal at the readings the rule uses, past one line on the daily reading | 3.28% of the fund's capital in 2 tranches
judgement.markdown:
- **Industry:** Arteche is in Industrials and capital goods. Industrials and capital goods' Industry RS was 46 at the Friday 23 October reading (73 four weeks earlier)
- **Sector:** Arteche is in Electrical equipment, grid and automation. That sector's Sector RS was 69 at the 30 September month-end; on Friday's daily reading it was 14
  - Arteche's sector's other companies, with their daily Stock RS: Alfen (16, a holding), Siemens (45), Schneider Electric (22), ABB (39), Siemens Energy (17), Legrand (23), and 10 more
- **Cohort:** Arteche is in Grid equipment makers for power networks. The cohort's relative strength was 28 on Friday's daily reading (42 four weeks earlier). Arteche's cohort's other companies: Alfen (16), Cembre (59), Landis+Gyr (52), Pfisterer (5), R&S Group Holding (8)
- **Arteche's charts are on Arteche's page on the PMS Per-stock Dashboard:** https://vfhqi.github.io/ratings/pms/holding.html?t=ART-ES

**What is going on, and why it matters**
- **The price move, by beta:** over twenty sessions Arteche's shares fell about 20%; Arteche's beta of 0.85 explains almost none of it, so Arteche's own move was about -20%, 1.1 times its usual size
- **The sector:** Arteche's sector's companies fell about 14% over the same twenty sessions, so most of the Arteche fall is the grid-equipment sector's fall, not Arteche's news; I found no Arteche company news this month
- **The analysts:** for Arteche, Net Upgrade Breadth, sales estimates and Net Upgrade Breadth, target prices were both +33% at the 30 September month-end, so the analysts were still raising Arteche's estimates as the price fell

**What it means for the position**
- **Holding:** hold Arteche to the 30 October reading; no Sell Criterion is met at the 30 September month-end
- **Selling:** on Friday's daily reading Arteche's price relative to the market is about 35% below its 52-week high, past the 25% line; *unless Arteche's relative price recovers about 13% in five sessions, the whole Arteche holding is sold at the 3 November session.* I put that as very likely
- **Adding:** no add; a whole-holding sell signal this close rules an add out

**What we could lose:** about 0.41% of the fund's capital, if Arteche's price falls to its 30% level at about EUR 26.39, about 12% below Friday's close of EUR 30.10

**Experiment: which stocks Arteche's own moves have tracked** (last 3 and 6 months)
- **Siemens Energy** (same sector): 0.43 and 0.25, moderate
- **ABB** (same sector): 0.40 and 0.22, moderate
- **Siemens** (same sector): 0.35 and 0.28, moderate
- **Legrand** (same sector): 0.34 and 0.35, moderate
- **My reading:** Arteche trades with the large grid-equipment makers, so the sector's mood sets Arteche's price this month; look at Siemens Energy first

**The Investment Analyst's memo on Arteche (1 October; no digest yet, so read from the memo's summary table and verdict)**
- **Decided:** the memo on Arteche is neutral on the shares and bullish on the business, and parks the case on price with medium conviction
- **Must happen:** the Strategic Plan 2030 presentation (October or November 2026) setting targets the market believes, and 2026 guidance of EUR 565 million to EUR 590 million of revenue delivered
- **Main risk:** valuation: the forward price-to-earnings ratio sat at the top of Arteche's own ten-year history when the memo was written
- **Expected return (the Modal return):** below our bar of 20% a year at EUR 29.50; the memo's price trigger is about EUR 22, about 27% below Friday's close
- **Next test:** the 30 October month-end reading, and the Strategic Plan 2030 presentation, which I have not found announced

**My judgement:** bearish on the Arteche position, medium to high conviction
- Arteche's relative price is far past the line the rule reads on 30 October, the sector is falling, and the memo's own buying price is a quarter lower
- **Counter-case:** the analysts are still raising Arteche's estimates and Arteche's Stock RS was 83 on Friday's daily reading, so the rule may sell a strong company in a sector-wide correction

**What would change my view:** a recovery of Arteche's relative price inside the 25% line by 30 October; the Strategic Plan 2030 presentation, if it comes first

items.criterion: MA SLs: each tranche's MA less 2%, information only for a Middle Innings Core Investment

bullets.text: Arteche is a Middle Innings Core Investment, so its MA SLs sell nothing; its six Sell Criteria decide the sale.
Arteche's tranche 2 had a 50D MA SL exit confirmed on 19-Aug, and Arteche closed 0.9% below tranche 2's €31.60 stop on 28-Oct.
Arteche's cushion above tranche 1's 200D MA SL (€30.09 on 27-Oct) fell from 29.7% on 29-Sep to 4.7% on 27-Oct, inside Arteche's usual 7.6% weekly move.

items.criterion: Relative price more than 25% below its 52W high, read at the month-end

bullets.text: No sell signal yet, but one is very probable at the 30-Oct month-end: Arteche's relative price was 33.3% below its 52W high on 28-Oct.
Avoiding the sell signal needs an Arteche close of about €35.20 on Friday 30-Oct at a flat market, 12.5% above Arteche's €31.3 close of 28-Oct.
If Arteche's relative price is more than 25% below its 52W high at the 30-Oct month-end, the rules sell the whole Arteche holding (3.28% of capital) on Tuesday 3-Nov.

items.criterion: Sector RS below 50 with Stock RS below 70, read at the month-end

bullets.text: No sell signal yet: Arteche's Sector RS (Electrical equipment, grid and automation) was 20 on 27-Oct, below 50, but Arteche's Stock RS was 87, above 70.
A sell signal needs Arteche's Stock RS below 70 on Friday 30-Oct with Arteche's Sector RS still below 50; otherwise Arteche's next reading is the 30-Nov month-end.
A Sector RS with Stock RS sell signal on 30-Oct would sell the whole Arteche holding on Tuesday 3-Nov, the same sale Arteche's relative price very probably brings.

items.criterion: Industry RS below 30, read each Friday

bullets.text: No sell signal: Arteche's Industry RS (Industrials and capital goods) was 53 on 27-Oct, up from 46 on 23-Oct, against a line of 30.
A sell signal needs Arteche's Industry RS to fall about four places among the 16 industries, below its 12-month low of 40 (March 2026).
An Industry RS sell signal for Arteche on a Friday would sell the whole Arteche holding at the next Tuesday session.

items.criterion: A tranche 30% below its highest close since purchase, with Stock RS below 70

bullets.text: No sell signal: both Arteche tranches' level of €26.39, 30% below the €37.7 high of 30-Sep, is 16.2% below Arteche's €31.5 close of 27-Oct.
A sell signal needs Arteche to break decisively below its rising 200D MA (€30.71 on 27-Oct) and Arteche's Stock RS (87) to fall below 70.

items.criterion: Stock RS below 50 with revenue or PT Net Upgrade Breadth below zero, read at the month-end

bullets.text: No sell signal: Arteche's Stock RS was 87 on 27-Oct, far above 50, and Arteche's revenue and PT Net Upgrade Breadth were both +33%.
Arteche's revenue and PT Net Upgrade Breadth held at +33% since 30-Sep, through a 20.2% fall in Arteche's SP to 23-Oct.
Arteche's analysts tend to follow the SP with their PTs, so a first Arteche PT cut would be the first crack; Arteche's Strategic Plan 2030 presentation is the next test.

items.criterion: The 200D MA of relative price flat or falling over the month, read each Friday

bullets.text: No sell signal: Arteche's relative 200D MA rose 3.3% over the month to 27-Oct, far from flat or falling at the Friday 30-Oct reading.
Low: Arteche's relative 200D MA would first stop rising in mid-February 2027 at the current relative price, or 20-Nov even with Arteche at about €23.5.

adds.criterion: The rules: no sell signal from the six Sell Criteria

bullets.text: No sell signal from any of the six Sell Criteria for Arteche at its last formal readings, Friday 23-Oct and the 30-Sep month-end.
At the 30-Sep month-end Arteche's Stock RS was 95, revenue and PT Net Upgrade Breadth +33% each, and relative price 18.8% below its 52W high.
Unless Arteche closes at about €35.20 by the 30-Oct month-end, Arteche's relative price (33.3% below its 52W high) gives a sell signal, blocking adds and selling the whole holding.

adds.criterion: The rules: room below the holding's limit

bullets.text: Arteche is 3.28% of capital against the 6.68% limit for a Middle Innings Core Investment, leaving 3.40% of room, enough for two 1.67% tranches.
The 6.68% limit only stops adds to Arteche and never forces a sale of Arteche.
Two 1.67% tranches would take Arteche to 6.62% of capital, just under the 6.68% limit.

adds.criterion: Your add trigger: a positive retest of a rising MA

bullets.text: Arteche held its rising 200D MA, closing at most 1.7% below that MA from 22 to 26-Oct and 2.6% above that MA at €31.5 on 27-Oct.
Your 28-Oct note says Arteche "has successfully retested the rising 200D MA today", but Arteche closed more than 2% below its rising 50D and 150D MAs from 22 to 27-Oct.
An Arteche close above its 50D MA (€32.19 on 27-Oct) would strengthen the setup; three Arteche closes below €30.09 would turn the 200D MA retest into a failure.

adds.criterion: Your add trigger: a broadening of the case (momentum rising in guidance, sell-side estimates, technicals or peers)

bullets.text: Arteche's case is not broadening: Arteche's sell-side estimates were flat over the month, Arteche's Stock RS eased and Arteche's large sector peers' Stock RS fell sharply.
Arteche's Stock RS was 87 on 28-Oct against 95 at 30-Sep, while Schneider Electric's Stock RS fell to 24 (from 68), ABB's to 45 (70) and Siemens Energy's to 26 (50).
Arteche's Strategic Plan 2030 presentation, scheduled for October or November 2026 but not yet dated, is the next chance for Arteche's estimates to rise.
Your 28-Oct note calls falling FY 2028 EPS estimates for Arteche a "MAJOR ISSUE" ("Ditto EBITDA") and Arteche's month-end relative price trigger a "MAJOR PROBLEM".
Arteche's FY2028 EPS consensus was 1.56 on 28-Oct, unchanged since 30-Sep but 1.3% below the 1.58 of 31-Mar, and Arteche's FY2028 EBITDA consensus followed a similar path.
Your 28-Oct note says Arteche "has successfully retested the rising 200D MA today", but Arteche's relative price very probably gives a sell signal first, at the 30-Oct month-end.
